message.reasoning:
I'm weighing whether to buy Electric Company despite my limited cash. GPT already owns Water Works, so if they acquire Electric Company too, they'd lock in a utility monopoly with 10x rent multiplier—a serious threat. My own cash position is weak at $67, and a lone utility only generates 4x rent on dice rolls, which isn't much. Still, blocking GPT from that monopoly has strategic value even if the purchase doesn't directly help me. GPT has significantly more capital at $670, so they're in a stronger position to make this move.

I'm torn between preserving my cash for building and pushing the price up to drain GPT's resources. A modest bid around $20-$30 could force them to commit more while keeping my risk manageable—if the price climbs past $50, I'll drop out. Winning Electric Company cheaply would be a steal compared to its normal $150 cost, and even a single utility generates some income. But my cash is tight, and overpaying would hurt my development strategy. I think I'll make a token bid to drive up the cost for GPT, but stay disciplined about my exit point.
